b2-kavehazikultura-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Writers Chose the Coffeehouse
b2-kavehazikultura-01.scenario: In a Budapest coffeehouse, a visitor asks you why young writers around 1900 spent their days in cafés, and how the coffeehouse differed from the salons.
b2-kavehazikultura-01.prompt: Tell her about the young journalists, and say how the coffeehouse differed from the salons.
cues: Say what the young journalists could not afford
Contrast the salons with the coffeehouse
b2-kavehazikultura-01.target: Ami a fiatal újságírókat illeti, sokuknak saját fűtött szobára sem tellett. A szalonok zárt társaságok voltak, a kávéház viszont mindenki előtt nyitva állt.
b2-kavehazikultura-01.english: As for the young journalists, many of them could not even afford a heated room of their own. The salons were closed circles; the coffeehouse, by contrast, stood open to everyone.
b2-kavehazikultura-01.canDo: I can describe the social and literary role of turn-of-the-century Budapest coffeehouses.

b2-kavehazikultura-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Nyugat Differed
b2-kavehazikultura-02.scenario: At the Centrál, a visitor asks you what made the new journal Nyugat different from the mass press in 1908.
b2-kavehazikultura-02.prompt: Tell her how Nyugat differed from the mass press and when the first issue appeared.
cues: Say what the mass press looked for and what Nyugat looked for
Say when the first issue appeared
b2-kavehazikultura-02.target: Míg a korabeli tömegsajtó a gyors szenzációt kereste, addig a Nyugat a minőséget kereste. Az első szám 1908. január elsején jelent meg.
b2-kavehazikultura-02.english: While the mass press of the time sought quick sensation, Nyugat sought quality. The first issue appeared on 1 January 1908.
b2-kavehazikultura-02.canDo: I can explain the historical significance of the founding of Nyugat in January 1908.

b2-kavehazikultura-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Strict Editor
b2-kavehazikultura-03.scenario: In the New York Café, a young poet asks you what kind of editor Ernő Osvát was.
b2-kavehazikultura-03.prompt: Tell her which manuscripts Osvát accepted and whom he discovered.
cues: Say what kind of manuscript he accepted
b2-kavehazikultura-03.target: Osvát csak a tökéletes kéziratot fogadta el. Éppen ő fedezte fel Móricz Zsigmondot.
b2-kavehazikultura-03.english: Osvát accepted only the perfect manuscript. It was precisely he who discovered Zsigmond Móricz.
b2-kavehazikultura-03.canDo: I can describe Ernő Osvát's editorial standard and say whom he discovered.

b2-kavehazikultura-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Argument over Ady
b2-kavehazikultura-04.scenario: At a literary evening in a Budapest coffeehouse, a guest asks you what the argument over Ady's Új versek was really about.
b2-kavehazikultura-04.prompt: Tell her what the debate was not merely about, and what the modernists said about Ady's poetry.
cues: Say what the debate was not merely about
Give the modernists' two points about Ady's poetry
b2-kavehazikultura-04.target: A vita korántsem pusztán verstani kérdésekről szólt. A modernisták szerint Ady költészete egyrészt a kuruc énekekből táplálkozott, másrészt a modern nagyvárosi ember szorongásait fejezte ki.
b2-kavehazikultura-04.english: The debate was by no means merely about questions of versification. According to the modernists, Ady's poetry drew on the one hand on Kuruc songs, and on the other expressed the anxieties of modern urban man.
b2-kavehazikultura-04.canDo: I can describe the public debate around Endre Ady's Új versek and the Nyugat writers.

b2-kavehazikultura-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What Happened to the Cafés
b2-kavehazikultura-05.scenario: In the Hadik Café in Buda, a student asks you what happened to Budapest's coffeehouses in the twentieth century.
b2-kavehazikultura-05.prompt: Tell her what happened to the coffeehouses in the 1950s and what began after the change of regime.
cues: Say what happened to most coffeehouses in the 1950s
Say what began after the change of regime
b2-kavehazikultura-05.target: Ami az ötvenes éveket illeti, a kávéházak többségét bezárták. A rendszerváltás után viszont megkezdődött a történelmi kávéházak újjászületése.
b2-kavehazikultura-05.english: As for the 1950s, most of the coffeehouses were closed. After the change of regime, however, the rebirth of the historic coffeehouses began.
b2-kavehazikultura-05.canDo: I can trace the fate of Budapest's coffeehouse culture through the 20th century and its revival after 1989.

b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Story of Nyugat
b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.scenario: At the New York Café, a visiting student asks you to sum up the story of Nyugat and its strict editor.
b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.prompt: Tell her how Nyugat differed from the official critics, and what Osvát demanded of a manuscript.
cues: Contrast the official critics with Nyugat
b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.target: Míg a hivatalos kritika a hagyomány ismétlését várta el, addig a Nyugat az alkotói szabadságot hirdette. Osvát csak a tökéletes kéziratot fogadta el.
b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.english: Whereas official criticism expected the repetition of tradition, Nyugat proclaimed creative freedom. Osvát accepted only the perfect manuscript.
b2-kavehazikultura-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the history of Budapest's literary coffeehouses and the review Nyugat (1908–1941).
